x-invitation-policy.backendTokenTransport: POST JSON body only; never URL paths or query strings
x-invitation-policy.fragmentLifecycle: Clear fragment after success; never log the fragment or invitation token
x-invitation-policy.tokenGeneration: 32 cryptographically random bytes encoded as unpadded Base64URL
x-invitation-policy.persistence: Store only SHA-256(token); never persist plaintext token in receipts or logs, or expose it in list responses or errors
x-invitation-policy.oneTimeResponse: 201 returns plaintext token once; identical retry is 200 with token:null even if invitation was later used or revoked
x-invitation-policy.managementVersion: campaign.version is independent of scene/token versions; membership/invitation mutations increment once, no-op/replay does not
x-invitation-policy.locking: Serialize invitation/member changes using campaign row lock; claim invitation and membership atomically
x-invitation-policy.replayAfterRemoval: Consumed-token replay succeeds only for its original actor while still a current member; never restore removed access
x-invitation-policy.bootstrap: Operator-only optional BOOTSTRAP_USERNAME and BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD; supply both or neither, validate strictly, never reset existing account/password/permissions

x-scene-policy.managementVersion: campaign.version is shared with P01; independent of scene and token versions. Successful create/activate increments once, including already-current activation; replay never increments.
x-scene-policy.receiptNamespace: One durable namespace shared by create and activate, separate from account and movement receipts; fingerprint contains command kind, campaignId, target sceneId or trimmed name, and expectedVersion.
x-scene-policy.atomicity: Scene command, campaign version and receipt commit atomically; parallel commands using the same expectedVersion have one winner, identical concurrent retries have one effect.
x-scene-policy.visibility: Inactive scene IDs and names are DM preparation metadata and never enter player snapshots, errors or events; no scene-by-ID read endpoint.
x-scene-policy.historicalReplay: Activation receipt is historical confirmation; refresh the current snapshot and list instead of treating the returned scene ID as current.
x-scene-policy.movement: Only tokens in the current scene can move, including receipt replay; inactive and foreign tokens return 404. Returning preserves positions, token/scene versions, controls and durable movement receipts.
x-scene-policy.realtime: After commit send private SCENE_CHANGED invalidation containing only type and campaignId. Reconnect and periodic reads recover missed switches.
x-scene-policy.clientLifecycle: On scene change clear old selection and failed movement retry; ignore old in-flight movement responses. Retain scene command requestId/body for explicit retry after ambiguous transport/5xx; refresh version on 409; clear map and management data on 401/403, including delayed successes.
x-scene-policy.migration: V3 preserves V1/V2 checksums and scene/token/receipt data, removes single-scene uniqueness and backfills a current-scene pointer constrained to the same campaign; initialization sets pointer transactionally and never resets an existing one.

x-asset-policy.storage: Stable UUID asset IDs and independent server-generated opaque storage keys. Publish files atomically before metadata commits in the configured private persistent root; never expose paths, keys or original filenames. Process crash may leave an unreferenced opaque file, which cannot be downloaded without committed metadata.
x-asset-policy.atomicity: On file, database or receipt failure rollback metadata, references, versions and receipts; clean new files on normal failure. Never delete previously committed or referenced assets. An uncertain commit acknowledgment requires checking matching metadata after the transaction: acquire a fresh campaign lock to wait for the original server transaction, since an unlocked MVCC read cannot prove absence during commit; preserve committed files; preserve files if the database is unavailable; only clean when absence is confirmed. Return the original failure and resolve retry via the durable receipt. No automatic deletion in P02b.
x-asset-policy.locking: Acquire actor then campaign locks consistently with account/scene management commands. Identical concurrent retries have one effect and return the original receipt before stale version checks.
x-asset-policy.visibility: Existing snapshot payloads remain unchanged: no asset or map metadata reaches player snapshots or events. SCENE_CHANGED contains only type and campaignId, emitted after commit and never replay.
x-asset-policy.download: Reauthorize every content read after logout or membership revocation; no public route or signed URL. Download successes and failures use Cache-Control: no-store, private; no ETag/304.
x-asset-policy.map: Enforce same-campaign map references. An inactive scene may be configured without switching; logical scene gridSize, dimensions, token positions and controls are unchanged. Calibration gridSize is in image pixels. Every successful map assignment/calibration/detach atomically resets fog to fully covered.
x-asset-policy.historicalReplay: Historical map receipts never reattach earlier images; clients reread authoritative state after success. Upload advances campaign management version; map command advances only target scene version.
x-asset-policy.migration: V4 preserves V1 through V3 data and checksums; database constraint enforces same-campaign asset references.
x-asset-policy.clientLifecycle: Retain requestId and exact file/body on transport or 5xx uncertainty for explicit retry; clear on deterministic 4xx, refresh versions/state on 409. Revoke object URLs and clear private previews/pending commands on unmount, scene/campaign switch and 401/403. Late successes cannot restore cleared private data; handle concurrent authorization failures independently. Successful command with failed refresh must not claim synchronized current map.
x-asset-policy.deployment: ASSET_STORAGE_ROOT uses a dedicated persistent Compose volume; local default is outside source files and git-ignored. DB plus asset backup/retention is P09; player-safe derived images and Pixi interaction are P02d.

x-token-policy.versions: Create advances the target scene version shared with maps/movement once and starts token version at 0. Update shares token version with movement, advances token and scene versions once even for unchanged values. Campaign management version is independent.
x-token-policy.locking: Acquire actor then campaign locks consistently with account/scene/asset commands. Same-request concurrent retries have one effect; concurrent commands using the same version have one winner.
x-token-policy.atomicity: Persist token configuration, controllers, scene version and receipt atomically; failures roll back all state and no event is sent.
x-token-policy.receiptNamespace: The token-commands namespace covers create and update across campaigns; it is separate from account, scene, asset and movement receipts. Key is session actor plus requestId, actor never comes from request data.
x-token-policy.historicalReplay: Historical receipts never recreate tokens, restore earlier names/positions/visibility/controls or regrant removed members; clients reread authoritative tokens and shared scene after success.
x-token-policy.membership: Fresh commands require every controller to be a current campaign member; invalid membership returns generic 400 without account identity. Validate membership before expected version. Identical retries bypass controller membership and stale version checks after current DM authorization and target ownership checks. Controllers are exact usernames sorted for canonical responses and fingerprints.
x-token-policy.revocation: Member removal deletes controls campaign-wide and advances affected token and scene versions; rejoin and replay never restore those controls. Version advancement prevents stale authoring forms from silently regranting control after rejoin. Empty controllers revoke all explicit control; current DMs retain implicit control.
x-token-policy.movement: Check current membership, current-scene visibility and current control before any historical movement receipt. Revoked control returns 403; hidden, inactive or foreign tokens return generic 404 for players. Existing movement versions and durable receipts are retained.
x-token-policy.visibility: Hidden tokens are omitted entirely from player snapshots. Shared snapshots and token views remain unchanged: no hidden flag, controller list, hidden identity/name/position/count enters shared payloads, errors or events. Private authoring routes require current DM membership.
x-token-policy.realtime: Publish after-commit SCENE_CHANGED invalidation containing only type and campaignId to current members; historical replay sends no event.
x-token-policy.migration: V5 preserves all V1 through V4 rows and checksums, adds durable token receipts and same-campaign membership integrity for controls, with backfill of existing controls.
x-token-policy.clientLifecycle: Enable submission only after authoritative tokens and members load. On 409 discard the command and refresh versions. On transport/5xx uncertainty preserve the exact body and requestId for explicit retry and disable conflicting edits. Campaign/scene change or 401/403 clears private state and pending operations; delayed successes cannot restore cleared state. Same-scope authorization denial invalidates concurrent success. Refresh shared scene after revocation/hidden changes so selected or pending movement cannot restore old token visibility or control.

x-map-visibility-policy.pixels: Output dimensions are scene.width * scene.gridSize by scene.height * scene.gridSize. Use nearest-neighbor sampling only. Unrevealed player cells and out-of-source pixels are opaque black (RGB 0, alpha 255). Flatten source alpha onto black; encode a fresh PNG with no source metadata.
x-map-visibility-policy.sampling: For output pixel (px, py), source is (offsetX + floor(px * map.gridSize / scene.gridSize), offsetY + floor(py * map.gridSize / scene.gridSize)); out-of-source pixels are black. Interpolation must never blend covered source cells into revealed cells.
x-map-visibility-policy.visibility: Every scene is default fully covered; only explicitly revealed player cells sample the source. Players never receive original bytes, even with every cell revealed. DM receives the full calibrated image. Unit hiding/control remains independent: map reveal never reveals hidden tokens and covered cells never hide visible units.
x-map-visibility-policy.authorization: Reauthorize every read: current membership, current scene and exact current scene version under the same campaign lock as map/fog/source reads and image generation. No historical images or role-selecting query capability.
x-map-visibility-policy.cache: Every success/failure, including malformed, anonymous, revoked, missing and stale results uses Cache-Control: no-store, private and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. No ETag, Last-Modified, 304, Range/206, redirect or public URL; no derivative cache or disk derivatives. Conditional requests never bypass authorization.
x-map-visibility-policy.originals: Original content routes remain DM-only, including guessed or foreign IDs; no-store applies to success and failure. Never expose private storage as a static directory.
x-map-visibility-policy.reCover: Re-covering changes future responses and invalidates old scene/version URLs, but cannot retract previously delivered pixels saved by players. A read authorized before a concurrent change may finish delivering its then-public result; subsequent reads use new state.
x-map-visibility-policy.versions: Every successful map assignment, calibration or detach atomically resets fog to fully covered and advances the existing scene version once. Token visibility and control are unchanged. Fog uses the shared scene version with moves/maps/token authoring; campaign management version is independent.
x-map-visibility-policy.fog: Replace the whole distinct in-bounds integer cell set, at most width * height entries; canonical order is y then x. Empty means fully covered, and fog can be prepared without a map. Request JSON keys are exact and required, with no nulls.
x-map-visibility-policy.locking: Acquire actor then campaign locks for fog commands consistently with existing mutations. Identical concurrent retries have one effect; same-version concurrent commands have one winner.
x-map-visibility-policy.atomicity: Persist fog state, scene version and durable fog receipt atomically. A separate fog-commands namespace is keyed by session actor plus requestId; fingerprint includes campaign, scene, expectedVersion and canonical revealed set. Current DM and target ownership precede replay; identical retries return original confirmation before stale checks. Changed fingerprints return 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Historical confirmations never restore earlier fog.
x-map-visibility-policy.realtime: Publish only after-commit SCENE_CHANGED invalidations containing type and campaignId; no pixels, fog, hidden token data or image URLs in events/errors. Replays cause no new event.
x-map-visibility-policy.migration: V6 introduces fog and fog receipts while preserving V1 through V5 checksums and old rows.
x-map-visibility-policy.clientLifecycle: Use cache: no-store for current map-view and image reads. On scene/version invalidation remove old image before requesting replacement; revoke object URLs and destroy textures on replacement, unmount, campaign/scene switch and 401/403, including concurrent image denials. Ignore late responses for disposed state. Reconnect and periodic reads reread maps. Retain exact body/requestId after uncertain POST, disable conflicting edits, preserve original draft version, and require latest post-ack authoritative read before claiming synchronization.
x-map-visibility-policy.interaction: Native Pixi pointer pan, cursor-centered wheel zoom/reset, selected-token drag preview and integer-cell snapping, click movement and two-point Euclidean distance times distancePerCell. Numeric movement fallback remains. DM rectangular reveal/cover and coordinate forms require explicit save and authoritative confirmation. This is geometric assistance, not a D&D movement rule.
